summary: Pieter Jacob Cosijn was a linguist who studied at Utrecht University from around 1860 to 1865. He later held a post at Leiden University from 1877 to 1899 and taught Christianus Cornelis Uhlenbeck.

Pietro Merlo was a linguist and Indologist who studied at the University of Turin under Giovanni Flechia and Giovanni Maria Bertini. He held posts at the University of Naples Federico II and the University of Pavia, becoming an ordinary professor in 1885.
Ping-kun Chen is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. He earned his doctorate from National Taiwan University (2001–2010) and became an assistant professor there in 2012.

Piotr Balcerowicz is an Indologist and philosopher who studied at Banaras Hindu University, the University of Warsaw, the University of Hamburg, and the Polish Academy of Sciences. He has served as a professor at Warsaw and SWPS University, alongside multiple visiting professorships.

Piotr Klafkowski was a scholar in Tibetology and linguistics who earned his PhD at Adam Mickiewicz University in Poznań under Jerzy Bańczerowski. He also studied under Lozang Jamspal, Geshe Geleg Gyatsho, and Nyalo Tulku Jampa Kelzang Rinpoche.

Piyanjali de Zoysa works in religious and Buddhist studies. After studying at the University of Delhi and the University of Colombo, she held an appointment at the University of Colombo as Professor in Clinical Psychology beginning in 1997.

Po Lu Khenpo Dorjé was a figure in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö. He taught Taklung Tsetrul Rinpoche and Chagdud Tulku Rinpoche.

Poerbatjaraka was an Indonesian linguist, Indologist, and archaeologist who studied under Nicolaas Johannes Krom at Leiden University. He served at the National Museum of Indonesia and held professorships at Gadjah Mada University, the University of Indonesia, and Udayana University.

Polly Young-Eisendrath is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who completed degrees at Goddard College and Washington University in St. Louis and undertook Zen training under Philip Kapleau. In 1994, she became a clinical associate professor of psychiatry at the University of Vermont.

Pongsit Pangsrivongse is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at the University of Cambridge and the University of Oxford. A former diplomat, he was appointed University Assistant of Pre-Modern South Asian Studies at the University of Vienna in 2025.
Pooja Tomar works in philosophy and Indology, having studied at the University of Delhi and Shri Mata Vaishno Devi University, where she earned her PhD in 2022 and served as a research scholar.

Popatbhai Ambashankar Mankad worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. His posts included State Engineer in Junagadh, Chief Engineer in Jodhpur State, and Chief Officer and Engineer for the Hyderabad Municipality.
Pori Park is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied under Robert E. Buswell Jr. She held a position as assistant professor of religious studies at Arizona State University.

Potprecha Cholvijarn is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied under Rupert Gethin and earned degrees from Bristol and Chulalongkorn University. At Chulalongkorn, he has served as a special lecturer and became Chair of Thai Studies in 2024.

Poul Tuxen was an Indologist and philosopher who studied under Ernst Windisch, Hermann Jacobi, and Dines Andersen at Copenhagen, Leipzig, and Bonn. In 1928, he succeeded Andersen as Professor of Indology at the University of Copenhagen, serving until 1951.
Poulami Ray is a historian and archaeologist who studied under doctoral supervisor Ranjit Sen. She is attested as a research scholar and fellow at The Asiatic Society in 2026.

Prabal Kumar Sen is a scholar of philosophy and Indology. He held an appointment as a professor at the University of Calcutta, attested in 2009, and held a post at the Ramakrishna Mission Institute of Culture.
Prabhasa Dharma was a figure in Buddhist and religious studies who undertook traditional training under Joshu Sasaki beginning in 1967 and under Seikaku Hirata.

Prabodh Chandra Bagchi was an Indologist, sinologist, and Buddhist studies scholar who earned a doctorate at the University of Paris under Sylvain Lévi. He held professorships and research directorships at the University of Calcutta, Peking University, and Visva-Bharati University.
Prabodh Shirvalkar is an archaeologist and Indologist who earned his PhD in 2009 at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute, where he was appointed assistant professor the same year.
